label: late "y" input in sequences starting with h/g/b/i
explanation: Sparse feature (about 0.025% of steps) that fires only in the original phase and on the delimiter, at steps 4-9, mostly in the last 1-3 original positions. Inputting "y" there carries 60% of the activation mass (lift 16x), and "y" gives every top activation. It depends heavily on the prefix: activation is much stronger when the first token is h (lift 16x; then g, b, i) and when z, o or 2 appeared just before, as in top examples like "h g e z o 2 [y]". Many of these steps are also followed by a smaller activation on <DEL> or the next token. It never fires in the copy phase or at t<3. A bare "y" input fires rarely (precision 0.4%), so the feature reads a specific hidden-state context rather than the token alone. Many weak activations on non-y tokens in similar h/g-initial prefixes are not captured. The best simple predicate reaches only F1 about 0.2.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=h (+6.43), orig0=g (+3.87), orig1=g (+3.62), orig0=b (+3.54), orig1=e (+3.54), orig2=z (+3.40). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.83), prev3_tok=- (-4.22), t=3 (-3.50), t=4 (-3.01).
